minutes.headline: School Committee voted to open hybrid, require masks prek-12, and ratified a one-year teachers' contract.
minutes.summary: Remote meeting began with an executive session on union negotiations, then public comment on reopening, masks and the hybrid schedule. The committee ratified a one-year LEA contract, revised the calendar to front-load ten staff days, accepted the personnel report, and heard a long reopening presentation. It then voted on masks, the hybrid model and quarterly registration for remote and bus families.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to open the 2020-21 school year in a hybrid model, as the superintendent recommended, passing 5-0 by roll call.
The committee voted 5-0 to make face coverings mandatory for students in prek through grade 12.
It voted 5-0 to require remote families to register quarterly and bus families to register for transportation.
The committee ratified a one-year LEA teachers' contract, 6-0 by roll call including the town manager.
The committee adopted a revised school calendar 5-0, deferring prek and kindergarten start to September 29 and asking for a later recommendation on professional development days.

why_it_matters: The hybrid model, mask rule and registration requirements set how and when children attend school and ride buses this fall, and they affect family schedules and child care.

The one-year teachers' contract adds salary and coach-pay costs to the school budget, and the committee heard that grants are expected to cover the reopening plan. A finance committee liaison asked for a review of budget effects since town meeting.
watch_next: The superintendent is to return by the end of September with a recommendation on placing professional development days.
Remote students joining sports is deferred until the MIAA decides; the committee added it as a future topic.
